data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The decentralized network is fundamentally more resilient to correlated failure than a redundant monolith because it trades 'redundancy' for 'heterogeneity', transforming systemic risks into localized faults.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services share a critical, single-point-of-failure upstream dependency (e.g., a single DNS provider or cloud region).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'independence' of the services is illusory due to shared software supply chains (e.g., all services using the same vulnerable library version).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Operational heterogeneity (as proposed in SRC_007) ensures that identical triggers (e.g., a specific kernel bug or Leap Second event mentioned in SCR_001) do not produce identical failure responses across the network, whereas a monolith with high internal redundancy often employs homogeneous stacks, creating a single point of failure across all redundant nodes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
